Meridian Ratings Affirms Saltmarsh Waterworks at A Minus With Stable Outlook

17 August 2026 | Written by Mara Ternell

Meridian Ratings has affirmed Saltmarsh Waterworks’ long-term issuer rating at A minus with a stable outlook. The rating reflects steady demand, predictable regulated income and adequate funding for repairs. The company supplies drinking water to 284,000 households and businesses in and around Kestria’s capital.

Revenue reached KRN 418 million in the year to June, up 4.8% from the previous year. Cash generated from operations covered interest payments 5.2 times. Water lost through leaks fell to 18.6% from 20.1%, although older pipes in the eastern districts remain a significant maintenance cost.

The stable outlook assumes annual capital spending of about KRN 110 million and no substantial debt-funded expansion. Available cash and committed borrowing facilities cover debt falling due over the next 18 months. A sustained increase in debt without matching earnings growth could put pressure on the rating.

Kestrian Regional Banks Face Narrower Margins Despite Steady Loan Demand

24 August 2026 | Written by Elian Voss

Meridian Ratings expects profitability at Kestria’s regional banks to weaken modestly during the remainder of 2026 as deposit costs rise. Its review of eight rated lenders found that average net interest margins fell to 2.7% in June from 2.9% in December. The sector outlook remains stable.

Loans grew by 3.6% over the same period, led by small business borrowing in Ostara and residential lending around Saltmarsh. Customer deposits increased by 2.8%. Banks have offered higher rates on fixed-term accounts to retain savers, reducing the benefit of growth in interest income.

Arrears remain manageable, with loans more than 90 days overdue representing 1.8% of the reviewed portfolios. Construction borrowers account for much of the recent increase. Meridian expects lenders to maintain current capital buffers, but banks with concentrated property exposure have less room to absorb unexpected losses.

Meridian Assigns BBB Rating to Amberford Packaging With Stable Outlook

25 August 2026 | Written by Tomas Belwick

Meridian Ratings has assigned Amberford Packaging a first-time long-term issuer rating of BBB with a stable outlook. The company produces paper-based food containers and industrial wrapping at two plants in Amberford. Its established customer relationships support earnings, although exposure to pulp prices limits the rating.

Amberford Packaging reported revenue of KRN 762 million and operating profit before depreciation of KRN 126 million for the year to June. Its five largest customers accounted for 38% of sales. Contracts covering roughly two-thirds of revenue allow material cost increases to be passed through within three months.

The company plans to spend KRN 74 million on a replacement production line over the next year. Meridian expects net debt to remain below 2.8 times operating profit before depreciation. The stable outlook assumes the project stays within budget and customer demand remains broadly consistent with current orders.

Meridian Upgrades Kestrel Bay Savings After Stronger Capital and Lower Arrears

3 September 2026 | Written by Elian Voss

Meridian Ratings has upgraded Kestrel Bay Savings’ long-term issuer rating to A minus from BBB plus. The outlook is stable. The upgrade reflects a sustained improvement in capital and loan quality, supported by retained earnings and a reduction in lending to speculative property developments.

The bank’s core capital ratio reached 15.4% at the end of June, compared with 13.6% a year earlier. Loans more than 90 days overdue declined to 1.2% of gross lending from 2.0%. Customer deposits funded 86% of loans, limiting reliance on borrowing from financial markets.

These improvements give the bank greater capacity to withstand the margin pressure affecting Kestrian regional lenders. Meridian nevertheless expects earnings growth to slow as savings rates rise. The stable outlook assumes that management maintains its current lending standards and does not materially increase distributions to shareholders.

Meridian Rates Saltmarsh Waterworks Bond in Line With Issuer Rating

10 September 2026 | Written by Mara Ternell

Meridian Ratings has assigned an A minus rating to Saltmarsh Waterworks’ proposed KRN 180 million senior unsecured bond. The issue rating matches the company’s long-term issuer rating, which remains A minus with a stable outlook. The bond is expected to mature in September 2033.

The company intends to use KRN 120 million of the proceeds to repay a bank loan due in February 2027. The balance will fund pipe replacement and treatment equipment within its existing investment programme. The transaction would extend debt maturities while leaving total borrowing within Meridian’s previous forecasts.

The proposed bonds will rank equally with the company’s other senior unsecured obligations. Meridian’s assessment assumes that the final terms are consistent with the draft documents reviewed. Cost overruns or a material increase in borrowing beyond the current programme could weaken financial headroom, but neither is included in the base forecast.

Ostara Homes Outlook Turns Negative as Sales Slow and Debt Rises

29 September 2026 | Written by Tomas Belwick

Meridian Ratings has revised the outlook on Ostara Homes to negative from stable and affirmed its BBB minus long-term issuer rating. Slower reservations and higher spending on land have increased borrowing. The company builds mid-priced homes in Ostara, Amberford and the outer districts of Saltmarsh.

Net reservations fell 14% in the eight months to August compared with the same period last year. Completed but unsold homes increased to 246 from 171 at December. Net debt reached KRN 392 million, equivalent to 3.7 times operating profit before depreciation over the preceding 12 months.

Cash and undrawn committed facilities total KRN 168 million, against KRN 61 million of debt due within a year. This supports the rating despite weaker trading. Meridian could lower the rating if inventory continues to build or net debt remains above four times operating profit before depreciation for a sustained period.

Val-Brume Heating Retains BBB Plus Rating Ahead of Winter Demand

5 October 2026 | Written by Céline Arvane

Meridian Ratings has affirmed Val-Brume Heating’s BBB plus long-term issuer rating with a stable outlook. The company provides district heating to 42,000 properties in Kestria’s French-speaking region. Its established network and contracted customer base support the rating, while seasonal cash needs and fuel costs remain constraints.

Fuel stocks at the end of September covered approximately 11 weeks of expected winter consumption. Fixed-price supply contracts cover 76% of forecast purchases through March 2027. The company also has an undrawn KRN 65 million revolving facility available to meet short-term working capital requirements.

Meridian expects operating cash flow to cover interest payments at least four times over the coming year. The forecast allows for routine maintenance and a KRN 28 million boiler replacement. An unusually prolonged cold period would increase purchases, but existing liquidity provides a reasonable buffer against that pressure.

Meridian Places Bracken Freight Under Review Following Proposed Harbour Acquisition

8 October 2026 | Written by Tomas Belwick

Meridian Ratings has placed Bracken Freight’s BBB long-term issuer rating under review for downgrade after the company announced an agreement to acquire Kestrel Bay Harbour Services. The proposed KRN 460 million purchase would expand Bracken’s storage and cargo handling operations but could materially increase debt.

Bracken has disclosed a committed bridge loan covering the full purchase price. It is also considering an equity issue, although the amount and timing have not been confirmed. Based on debt-only funding, Meridian estimates that net debt could exceed four times annual operating profit before depreciation immediately after completion.

The review will examine the final funding mix, integration costs and the acquired business’s cash generation. Bracken expects completion before the end of October, subject to the remaining transaction conditions. Meridian will resolve the review once it has sufficient evidence to assess the combined company’s financial position.

Kestrian Food Producers Maintain Stable Outlook as Input Costs Ease

9 October 2026 | Written by Céline Arvane

Meridian Ratings has maintained a stable outlook for Kestria’s packaged food sector. Lower grain and container costs are helping producers rebuild margins, although household spending remains subdued. Across six rated companies, average operating margins increased to 11.2% in the first half of 2026 from 10.4% a year earlier.

Sales volumes rose just 0.8%, with stronger demand for basic products offset by weaker purchases of premium lines. Producers supplying retailers in Saltmarsh and Amberford reported increased use of promotions. Meridian expects price competition to limit how much of the recent cost relief companies retain.

The sector’s median net debt stood at 2.4 times operating profit before depreciation at June. Most rated producers have sufficient cash and committed facilities for planned investment over the next year. Debt-funded acquisitions or prolonged discounting would create greater pressure than the modest volume growth currently assumed in Meridian’s forecasts.
